86.t: Ancestry, his Indian father and his mother Kitty's family
86.s: He knows little of family background: his father he barely saw, his grandmother was a slave, and he left Columbus at about 19.
86.q: Well, my dad was an Indian and, let’s see, my folks, their name was Schultz (spells it). In fact, there were so many of them in the little town in Kentucky, they call the town “Schultztown, Kentucky.” So, I never did delve in my family background. My mother used to tell me quite a bit about what a…

86.t: Born in Columbus, raised by uncle and aunt in Beaver Dam, Kentucky
86.s: Edison says no one in his family was musical; born in Columbus in 1915, he was sent to Kentucky at five when his grandmother died and his mother worked two jobs.
86.q: No, there wasn't anyone in the family musical but me. I had an uncle that raised me from the time I was five until I was twelve. He had an interest in music. Not professional but he just liked music and he used to -- he'd see an old instrument out in the garbage or anything; he'd pick it up and…

383.t: Birth in Austin and early schooling at Sam Houston College
383.s: Wilson gives his birthdate and parents' names, his brother Gus, and how his mother taught them to read so they entered school at four and five.
383.q: So I guess that a good place to start would be back to my earliest recollections as a child back in Austin, Texas. I was born in Austin, Texas on November 24, 1912, and my father's name was James Augustus Wilson, my mother was Pearl Georgia Shaw, her maiden name.

383.t: Staying with the Shaw grandparents in Montgomery before settling in Tuskegee
383.s: The family lives with his mother's parents in Montgomery while she waits for a Tuskegee post, then settles in Greenwood; he recalls his grandfather and his parents' origins.
383.q: Alabama, and my father got this job at Tuskegee Institute -- and Booker T. Washington was still President and founder of that school in Tuskegee.

234.t: Born in Toronto in 1912; mother, step-fathers and mining towns
234.s: Gil gives his birth date and place, then describes his wandering mother, her several husbands and a childhood in mining and lumber towns.
234.q: Well I had some brothers and sisters which I never knew because they were born before me and a couple of them died before I was born. (Mother was about 45 before I was born?).

234.t: Moving from Toronto through Florida, Spokane and Seattle
234.s: Gil recalls early moves, including a wild Florida hotel run by his mother around 1918.
234.q: I was very young at the time. I don't remember it too well. I only have impressions you know. We lived in Florida for a while. My mother was remarried in Florida. My first step-father was, his name was Gustin and they lived in Florida. My mother ran a little hotel on a road between two towns. I…

32.t: Birth, parents and siblings in South Carolina
32.s: White gives his birth date, parents, siblings, and his mother's work as a rural schoolteacher before he was placed in the Jenkins orphanage.
32.q: I was christened by Friday Montgomery Methodist preacher Amos Earl Mordecai White. Amos was all right. The Mordecai was quite complicated because the people in my early life used to call me Mordecai instead of Mordecai as it is properly pronounced. November 6, 1889 was given in the Bible as my date…

776.t: The Streckfus brothers, the family business and the first boat's trio
776.s: Verne names his brothers, his father's 1895 start and the 1903 steamer J.S.; the first orchestra was pianist Charlie Mills's three-piece group.
776.q: Well, that was Joe, which is the oldest. And Roy's second, John third, and then on fourth. And H. Was your father? Father started the business in 1895. And built the first excursion boat that was used exclusively for one-day excursions, the steamer JS, built in 1903. And at that time, it was run on…

648.t: Birth, church and orphaned childhood in New Orleans
648.s: Born 1890; family church; parents died when he was twelve and Tom fourteen; night school.
648.q: I was born in January of 13, 1890, in New Orleans. And, uh, there was five of us born in New Orleans. Mm-hmm. We were all Christian and practically the same church, Father Lambert's church. That's a Catholic church. Yeah, Father, uh, Father.

194.t: His father and mother, and the move from Bogalusa
194.s: Longhair says his mother brought him to New Orleans at about two months old; he never knew his father James Lucius Byrd, and his mother Ella Mae Byrd was born in Brookhaven.
194.ch: Family and downtown New Orleans childhood
194.q: No, really I don't. I really don't. Like I said, I don't know too much about him, you know, at all.

303.t: His mother and photographs at home
303.s: Riddick's mother was a Cincinnati piano graduate who died at 39 in 1918.
303.ch: Scrapbook: family, baseball and musician friends
303.q: His mother was a graduate of Cincinnati, a conceptual of music, and her degree was for piano. Passed away at the early age of 39 years old back in 1918.

708.t: Family's move to Chicago in 1915 and the start of her entertainment career
708.s: Her family moved to Chicago in 1915. She had no music connection until much later; making records was her entry into entertainment.
708.q: Yes, long after. Now, the first of my starting to in the entertainment world was making those records.

488.s: His family's North Carolina and Chicago roots, long-lived grandparents and a story of his grandmother.
488.q: Yes. Yeah my father came from North Carolina, my mother was born outside of Chicago in Maywood, Illinois. And you know, my grandfather had been a chef on the Chicago Northwestern Railroad. So he was used to traveling back and forth from California and whatnot. And I didn’t really know my paternal…

678.s: His home town in Fife, a Scottish county called a Kingdom, which he left at 17 or 18.
678.q: Cowdenbealth is about maybe 20 miles northeast of Edinburgh. It’s in Fife actually. It’s over the other side of the Forth Bridge. And it’s in the Kingdom of Fife. And that’s the only County in Scotland that’s actually called a Kingdom. So I grew up there, but I left there when I was like 17 or 18,…

417.t: Birth, mother Irma, and meeting his father Charles Evans
417.s: Born while his father was in World War II, Benson first met his father at four; he describes his poor but happy early life and his father's family.
417.q: As far as I know, my name is George Washington Benson. I was born in 1943, March the 22nd. I’m from Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. That’s my beloved home town. That’s my beginnings.

558.t: Birth in El Cerro, parents, siblings and father's factory job
558.s: Camero gives his birth date and place in Havana, his parents' and siblings' names, and says his father made soft-drink bottles while his mother stayed at home.
558.q: Candido Camero: Well, from my birth - I was born on Friday, April 22, 1921 at six thirty in the afternoon in El Cerro, one of the neighborhoods in the city of Havana, Cuba. My dad’s name is Candido Camero. My mom’s name is Caridad Guerra.

110.t: His mother's family: Betsy's emigration and organists
110.s: Little musical background on his mother's side except some church organists; his grandmother Betsy's route from White Russia and Poland to California.
110.ch: Family and boyhood in Concord and Ione
110.q: No. Not that I know of. That family you mentioned being Polish, trying to trace them, we’ve heard that they were in White Russia – her mother. Betsy. Her mother. Then into Poland, and from Poland to Germany, and from Germany she got a way to get to California as a nanny or a servant to the Gangerer…

16.t: Born in Kansas City, the Henderson name, Watonga and chautauquas
16.s: He was born in a Kansas City hospital while the family lived in Oklahoma; he speculates on the Henderson family origin and recalls Watonga; defines chautauqua.
16.q: Well we didn't actually move to Kansas City. We just took a little side trip. The way they used to tell it to me was kind of like, you know, a holiday weekend or something like that. We went over, they had me, and then they came back and so it didn't, we still lived in Oklahoma.

471.t: Parents and birth on Corcoran Street
471.s: Cobb names his parents, says he was born on Corcoran Street in northwest Washington, and describes summers at his mother's family tobacco farm in La Plata.
471.ch: Growing up and learning drums in Washington
471.q: My mother is Katherine Bivens Cobb, and my father is Wilbur Cobb. They met somewhere around before I was born and got married and had me. He’s from Carolina somewhere, and she’s from southern Maryland. How they got together, I’m not really sure about that. That’s how it happened. They tell me I was…

108.t: Family origins and the move to Colwyn
108.s: Wilder's parents' North Carolina and Pennsylvania roots, and his father's family settling in Colwyn, near Philadelphia, in 1912.
108.ch: Childhood and learning music in Philadelphia
108.q: My – I think – I know my father’s family are from North Carolina. I think my mother’s family were also from North Carolina. Apparently they had come North much earlier than my father’s family, because my mother was born in Pennsylvania. My father was born in North Carolina. He left – my grandfather…

372.t: Birth, name and immigrant parents in Chicago
372.s: Konitz gives his birth date, how Leon became Lee, his Austrian and Ukrainian parents, the laundry business and his two older brothers.
372.q: “Leon” was my given name and “Lee” has become my second name. The fact is that I had two older brothers and I was supposed to be a girl, and my name was going to be “Leonna”. So I became “Leon” and then after a while my friends called me “Leo”, and then “Lee”, and it’s going to “Le”. When I get to…

228.t: Maxton and Greensboro: North Carolina family and summers
228.s: Prompted by a question about the North Carolina migration stream, McLean recalls Maxton, his grandmother's house in Greensboro, cousins, his name Lenwood, the news of John McLean's death in 1939.
228.ch: Harlem youth, Monk and Bird, and Greensboro
228.q: First of all, my first recollections of North Carolina didn’t happen in Greensboro. When my mother first took me down, when I must have been about a year old, we went to a city, a little small place, called Maxton – M-a-x-t-o-n – North Carolina. There my grandmother had a little house. I can…

367.t: Parents' origins and the seven Young children
367.s: Young gives his father's Dayton roots, his mother's Virginia roots, and names his brothers and sisters.
367.q: My mother was from Virginia. I don‘t remember the name of the city or anything, but I know she was from Virginia. Her family moved to Ohio, I can‘t tell you too much about that because it was before I was born. So I do know that my mother was from Virginia.

377.t: The first Decca session and John Chilton's claim about his mother
377.s: Kuehl moves to the 1937 Decca session and a reference book claim that his mother was a pianist; Basie says she only played a little.
377.ch: Early career: vaudeville and Kansas City

87.t: His family and Savannah migrants to New York
87.s: He has sisters and half brothers, an uncle Will who played trombone, and says Savannah people went to New York as New Orleans people went to Chicago.
87.ch: Learning the trombone and jam sessions
87.q: Well, I had some half brothers, and then I had three sisters and some half brothers. I have two sisters living now. My half brothers are dead.

66.t: Leaving Atlanta, her mother's family and who was musical
66.s: She left Atlanta at 3 or 4. Her mother's family, including a great-grandmother, all came from Atlanta; only she and her mother were musical, apart from a twin brother who danced.
66.q: Until I was, I think, 3 or 4. It's difficult, it's been so long, to remember how old I was because I never heard them tell me how old I was when we left Atlanta. I think I was between 3 and 4.

70.t: His mother's and father's family origins
70.s: His mother came from London, Ohio, daughter of a horse trader; his father came from Danville, Kentucky.
70.ch: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
70.q: She was born in London, Ohio. Oh, maybe the town is about maybe 14 or 15 miles from Springfield going towards Columbus, that way. Just a very little town.

147.t: Orphaned in Memphis and raised by illiterate grandparents
147.s: Crawford recalls starting in high school in Memphis, losing his parents young and being raised by his grandparents, his grandmother a famed midwife.
147.ch: Memphis boyhood and the Ohio territory years
147.q: Well, Stanley, I started out in Memphis, Tennessee, in high school under Jimmy Lansford's band, and I'm going back around about '28 and '29 now, and so we formed a little amateur high school orchestra, and so -- well, I just knew I was going (Inaudible), my mother, dad died when I was six, five or…

233.t: Moving to Columbus at nine; no formal training in the family
233.s: After his parents separated the boys went to Columbus to be with their father and stayed ten years; June died there. None of the brothers had lessons.
233.q: No, not that I knew of, unless Buddy and Wes sneaked out somewhere, there was no formal training whatsoever. As I was explaining, about that period that we were in Columbus, at the age of 9...My folks had separated and at the age of 9 I was left...my mother...let me see. Wes and my older brother --…

384.t: Boyhood in Niagara Falls and Chambersburg; his pianist father
384.s: Born in Niagara Falls in 1902, he grew up partly in Chambersburg, Pennsylvania; his father was a store clerk and post office worker who played piano professionally, including in a theater.
384.ch: Kline 1980: early years and founding of the Goldkette orchestra
384.q: Went to Pennsylvania, yeah. And my father was working in Pennsylvania.

99.t: Birth in Argenta, parents, father's jobs and family hardship
99.s: Pillars was born in Argenta (North Little Rock), Arkansas in 1906, recalls his brother Charles's birth, and describes his father's work delivering flowers and then as a post office janitor.
99.q: Yes. I was born in North Little Rock, Arkansas. The town was called Argenta, Arkansas at the time of birth and in later years it was -- the name was changed to North Little Rock, Arkansas. April the 30th, 1906. I lived at 311 North 21st Street in North Little Rock.

169.t: Born in Oklahoma; mother and father die early
169.s: McGhee was born in Oklahoma, taken to Detroit, lost his mother, was sent to his grandmother in Haskell, and his father died when he was five; a store left for him came to nothing.
169.ch: Childhood and first music in Oklahoma
169.q: Right...and that's about it. [LAUGHS] No, I was born in Oklahoma, but my folks moved to Detroit, you know, when I was really young. In fact, my mother died in Detroit, because... See, she was only there for about a year before she died, so I didn't really get to know her. Then they decided to send…

236.t: Born in Spokane; stepfather and leaving for Los Angeles
236.s: Rowles was born in Spokane in 1918, his father died young and his stepfather wanted him to be a lawyer. At twenty-one he announced he was going to Los Angeles to play piano.
236.ch: Spokane and arrival in Los Angeles
236.q: My mother was. See, my father died when I was three months old. So I never had a father. I had a stepfather. And he was very un-musical. He wanted me to do all kinds of things that I didn't want to do, like caddie for him every Sunday, when I was a... I was a tennis player, and I don't mind saying…

239.t: Born in Memphis; father the college professor, move to Chicago
239.s: Born in Memphis, the family moves to Chicago when he is four or five; his father taught at Le Moine College and is honored there around 1927.
239.q: to Chicago. My father was a professor, an English professor, you know, at Le Moine (PHONETIC) College in Memphis. In fact he taught Jimmy Lunceford English, before Lunceford went to Fisk University in Nashville. And then we moved to Chicago when I was, oh, maybe five, four or five, right around the…

98.t: Born in Memphis, moving to Chicago in 1923, raised by his sister
98.s: Saunders was born in Memphis in 1912, lost his mother in 1919, and was raised by his much older sister, who moved the family to Chicago for work and passed for white.
98.ch: Childhood, first drums and the hustling years
98.q: Yeah, well, my sister raised me, you know. Earlier, my mother died, in 1919, and then my father, he left us and my sister raised me. So she became my mother and father.
